newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar closes flat after turbulence.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar closes flat after turbulence.

text.p: * Canada's dollar closed flat at C$1.3727 (0.7285) from Thursday's close of C$1.3730 (O.7284) after a roller coaster day spurred by new economic data, dealers said.
* They said Canadian unemployment numbers gave the unit support, but U.S. payroll data then sparked speculation of a rate hike in the United States, weakening the currency.
But when U.S. non-farm payroll numbers were released at 0830 EDT, market players speculated about a U.S. rate hike before the end of September, Gregory said.
August non-farm payrolls increased by 250,000 while the unemployment rate stood at around 5.1 percent.
Ecnomists surveyed by Reuters expected a 244,000 rise in payrolls and a 5.3 percent jobless rate.
"The market got very nervous and people began to sell," said Gregory. "We have yet to test the waters of the Bank of Canada's negative spread amid Fed rate hikes."
The Bank of Canada is expected to maintain low rates even if the U.S. Federal Reserves rases its rates, widening the negative spread, Gregory said.
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar rose to 1.0871 marks from Thursday's close of 1.0818 marks and held steady at 79.49 yen.
